sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: White spruce is a North American conifer, mainly of boreal and montane forests. It generally reaches about 30 m.

sections.title: Needles and cones
sections.text: The evergreen needles are attached singly and have four angles. The narrow cones hang from the branches. The plate is compatible with a spruce, but its visible features are not enough to distinguish this species from every other Picea.

sections.title: Nomenclature and uses
sections.text: North American forestry references use Picea glauca; the current POWO/WCVP treatment places it in synonymy with Picea laxa. Its wood is used for pulp and lumber.
